purpose: The narrow, read-only production scanner interface a future Build 6 candidate must preserve. Captured offline with the provider fetch intercepted; zero provider calls. Frozen: all later Phase 6 work operates from this snapshot, not from a live product tree.

scannerContract.imageInputShape: base64 JPEG inline_data; client re-encodes to 896px max dimension at quality 0.65; Edge Function refuses payloads over 2MB base64 before any provider call
scannerContract.singleDispatchState: single dispatch proven; one scan produces one provider call
scannerContract.rollbackSelector: certified-v140 is the active control; no candidate is registered in any product path, so rollback is the absence of a change rather than a switch

android.tipDeltaNote: f5fb946 adds an internal Supabase staging EAS profile. eas.json is in no scanner closure path, and the staging profile sets no scanner-candidate flag, so the pinned scanner identity is unchanged by it.

productSourceIdentity.inspectionMode: read-only. No product file was opened for write, and both protected worktrees were verified clean after capture.

certifiedControlComparison.rule: Historical results are reusable only when every recorded request, model, schema, sampling, parser, and contract identity is byte-identical.
certifiedControlComparison.interpretation: Provider payload, prompt, response schema, sampling, model and provider parser are byte-identical between certified-v140 and the current product. The request contract differs (the product dispatches legacy-selected-item, not V2) and the response contract differs (the product adds the identify_for_closet intent and three Closet entry paths in _shared/fashionIdentificationV2.ts). scan-identify/index.ts itself is byte-identical between certified-v140 and both current platform lines. Under the equivalence rule this is provider-payload equivalence only, which is explicitly insufficient for reuse.
